grammar.title: The five relative day words
grammar.pattern: 前天 / 昨天 / 今天 / 明天 / 后天
grammar.explanation: Chinese has a tidy set of words for days relative to today: 前天 ("the day before yesterday"), 昨天 ("yesterday"), 今天 ("today"), 明天 ("tomorrow"), 后天 ("the day after tomorrow"). Like other time words, they go at the start of the sentence or right after the subject.

grammar.title: 星期天 and 星期日 for Sunday
grammar.explanation: Unlike the numbered weekdays (星期一 through 星期六), Sunday breaks the pattern: it's 星期天 or, more formally, 星期日 — both mean the same thing and are used interchangeably.

sentences.en: I didn't go the day before yesterday.
Are you coming the day after tomorrow?

sentences.zh: 前天他没来，后天他能来。
sentences.pinyin: Qiántiān tā méi lái, hòutiān tā néng lái.
sentences.en: He didn't come the day before yesterday, but he can come the day after tomorrow.
